conviction_note: No company-level number the market has not seen. The name trades on the first FY27 guide from a CEO who started on 2026-07-29. The evidence splits two ways. Supporting a relief move: the street reset into the print with five target cuts on Oct 9-27 and two targets below spot, short interest rose 19% at the 10/30 settlement, and the closest peer (SMPL) rose 11.4% on a reset-plus-margin-path FY27 guide. Against it: a 14.7% 20-day run-up off the lows, three FY26 profit-guide cuts, 6 of the last 7 prints down, and the incentive for a new CEO to set a low bar. p_up 52 on an abs move of 17 gives +0.68. The findings sum to +0.40 and agree with that in sign and size.
bar: Q4 FY26 revenue consensus $653.2M with EPS $0.21 (Earnings Whispers preview, 2026-11-10, https://www.earningswhispers.com/article/BRBR/23122). Benzinga carries $655.6M and $0.23 (https://www.benzinga.com/quote/BRBR/charts). Chartmill's $669.6M and $0.24 is an outlier (https://www.chartmill.com/stock/quote/BRBR/estimates). The company guide implies Q4 sales of $629-669M (FY $2.335-2.375bn less 9M $1,706.4M), Q4 adj EBITDA margin ~10%, FY adj EBITDA $275-295M, and ~$7M of Q4 trade spend to clear excess bottles (Q3 release 8-K, 2026-08-04, https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001772016/000162828026052137/brbrexh991-q32026earningsr.htm). FY27 street, per S&P Global via stockanalysis.com (single source, so FY27-dependent findings are capped small): revenue $2.38B (+0.7%), adj EPS $1.31 (+25% on FY26 $1.04) (https://stockanalysis.com/stocks/brbr/forecast/, as of 2026-11-17). No FY27 EBITDA consensus found.

Not a crowded-squeeze setup like 18-23% of float, but a reason to keep negatives small.

expectations.real_bar: For the stock to rise, the FY27 outlook has to show adj EBITDA growing off the ~$285M FY26 base with a credible elasticity assumption (the street's FY27 EPS of $1.31 implies about +25%), with no new inventory charge and the Q4 margin at or above ~10%. The Q4 revenue number is secondary.

next_guide.street_full_year: FY27 revenue $2.38B, adj EPS $1.31 (S&P Global via https://stockanalysis.com/stocks/brbr/forecast/, 2026-11-17)
next_guide.company_current_guide: none for FY27. Qualitative only: FY27 adj EBITDA margins will improve on FY26 (~12%); ~120bp of FY26 inventory impacts should not recur; $10-12M of annualized opex savings, mostly in FY27; double-digit Premier shake price increase plus powder pricing, effective Q1 FY27; elasticity 'slightly greater than 1'; whey elevated through next year, milk protein inflation mid-single-digit (Q3 call, https://www.webull.com/news/15385459541566464)
next_guide.basis: Management committed on the Q3 call to giving the first FY27 guide on this call and to FY27 margin improvement. A new CEO plus three FY26 cuts make a conservative initiation more likely than one above a street that already models +25% EPS. The peer SMPL's reset guide on 2026-10-27 was conservative on sales and still bought.

findings.finding: The sell-side bar has been reset lower into the print. Five target cuts on Oct 9-27 (BofA Sell $10->$9, TD Cowen $12->$9, UBS $14->$9.50, Barclays $14->$12, JPM $18->$15) take the mean target to $13.35 and the low to $9, two of them below the $10.9 spot. The FY27 EPS consensus of $1.31 sits after these cuts, so the FY27 bar the guide is measured against has already been lowered.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Guidance line: the Nov 2025 initial FY26 guide brought +2.5%. The three FY26 guide cuts brought -14.4% (Feb), -38.8% (May) and -1.5% (Aug, by when cuts were expected). That pattern suggests a guide the street already expects to be low draws a damped reaction.
findings.why_not_priced: Partly priced: the stock fell to ~$9.5 around these cuts. What is not priced is the next step. If the market still held the pre-cut bar, the stock would trade near the old $14-18 targets, not $10.9 with two Holds/Sells at $9. A guide that merely meets the cut estimates clears a lowered bar.
findings.independence: Earnings Whispers' preview (https://www.earningswhispers.com/article/BRBR/23122) independently describes low expectations, with bearish sentiment at 56.5% against 44.4% before the last print.

findings.finding: The stock ran +14.67% over 20 days and +7.23% over 5 days into the print, from $9.49 (2026-10-27) and $9.62 (2026-11-09) to $10.905. Part of the relief a credible FY27 framework would bring is already in the price, which raises what the release has to show.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Run-up into a guide event: no earlier sourced instance for this name. The baseline shows 6 of 7 prints down with a median absolute move of 14.4%.
findings.why_not_priced: This is about the price itself, so it is priced by definition. What it says is that the bar for a positive reaction is higher than at the lows. If the market had not run, spot would still be around $9.5-9.6.
findings.independence: The sealed baseline's own run-up fields (yahoo bars) show the same move from a different source. Finding 1's target cuts point the other way and are a different fact (analyst estimates rather than price).

findings.finding: Shorts built into the print: shares short rose from 12.33M (2026-10-15) to 14.71M (2026-10-30), +19%. That is 3.88 days to cover and about 12.7% of shares outstanding, and the stock has since rallied about 13%, so the late shorts are under water. A credible FY27 guide could force covering.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No earlier squeeze on this name is sourced. Short interest was 11.9M in May 2026, when the print still fell 38.8%. A short is no floor when the guide is cut.
findings.why_not_priced: FINRA data lag. The 10/30 settlement printed in mid-November, and the rally since then may partly be covering, which would mean some fuel is already spent. If this were fully priced, the next settlement would show the short shrinking, and that is not yet observable.
findings.independence: ShortSqueeze shows ~12.25M short and 3.2 days to cover at 2026-10-27 (cited in search results). The sweep row shows 10.6% of float. Both rest on the same FINRA data, so they are not independent.

findings.finding: The first FY27 guide, from a new CEO, is the dominant line. The street has FY27 revenue at $2.38B (+0.7%) and adj EPS at $1.31 (+25%). Management promised only that margins improve on FY26's ~12%, citing ~120bp of non-recurring inventory hits, $10-12M of savings and a double-digit shake price. Against that: elasticity >1, mid-single-digit milk protein inflation, ~4x leverage raising interest, and a CEO who declined to say where margins settle. This makes a conservative initiation at or below +25% EPS somewhat more likely than one above it.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Guidance line: the initial FY26 guide (Nov 2025) brought +2.5%, then three cuts brought -14.4%, -38.8% and -1.5%. This line has moved the stock by double digits.
findings.why_not_priced: The FY27 numbers do not exist yet. The street figure comes from one aggregator and no FY27 EBITDA consensus is visible. If the market were confident in a +25% EPS year, the stock would sit nearer the $13 median target than at a ~8x forward multiple on $1.31.
findings.independence: Earnings Whispers' preview (https://www.earningswhispers.com/article/BRBR/23122) flags the risk of a 'fourth EBITDA reset'. The FY27 street figure is from https://stockanalysis.com/stocks/brbr/forecast/. Both are secondary sources. The guide-direction inference is mine and is capped small because the FY27 bar has a single source.

findings.finding: The closest listed peer, Simply Good Foods (Quest, OWYN, Atkins), guided FY27 on 2026-10-27 to sales -13% to -17% and adj EBITDA -9% to -14%, on a near-double-digit price increase and distribution losses, with 250-300bp of gross-margin recovery. Its Q4 retail takeaway was -8% (Quest -2%, OWYN -7%). The stock rose 11.4% on the day because the quarter beat and the guide gave a margin path. This is a template for how this market treats a reset guide with margin recovery in this sub-sector.
findings.link: Same protein-nutrition shelf and same club/mass channels (BellRing has just over 40% of sales in club). OWYN and Quest RTD shakes compete directly with Premier. Both companies are taking roughly double-digit price in FY27 against protein inflation. No shared-customer revenue figure available.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Not applicable to BRBR directly. SMPL's reaction is the analogue: a beat plus a reset guide that showed a margin path brought +11.4%.
findings.why_not_priced: Reaction transmission, not a fact about BRBR. BRBR's 14.7% 20-day run-up started after SMPL's print, so part of this may already sit in the price. Sized small as a proxy.
findings.independence: SMPL's 8-K press release (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001702744/000170274426000028/a991_pressreleasexq4x2026.htm) confirms the guide figures. Same event, so not independent of the reaction article.

findings.finding: Glanbia (Optimum Nutrition, the largest whey buyer) said on 2026-11-04 that WPC-80 prices peaked in Q3 and have fallen back to early-2026 levels, though they remain well above last year. It still expects input costs in early 2027 to be higher than in 2026. ON branded sales rose 25.8%, so protein demand is strong. That points to some easing in the protein-cost assumption behind BRBR's FY27 guide, mainly in H2.
findings.link: Glanbia/ON competes with Dymatize in protein powders and is a price-setter in whey. BellRing's shakes run mostly on milk protein (BRBR cited mid-single-digit milk protein inflation), so only partial cost transmission. No revenue link.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Cost line: protein inflation and freight drove the FY26 margin cuts (-38.8% May, -1.5% Aug).
findings.why_not_priced: Macro-to-company transmission that BRBR has not confirmed. BRBR covers about six months ahead, so the decline reaches FY27 H2 at best, which limits what it can do to the initial guide.
findings.independence: The Glanbia Q3 call highlights (https://www.marketbeat.com/instant-alerts/transcript-glanbia-q3-earnings-call-highlights-2026-11-04/) are the same event. Earlier June 2026 coverage of record WPC-80 prices (https://vespertool.com/news/wpc80-prices-at-record-levels-as-new-protein-demand-grows-faster-than-supply/) gives the peak context.

findings.finding: Director Shawn Conway bought 2,022 shares at $9.89 on 2026-09-08 (Form 4 code P, about $20k), taking his holding to 18,180 shares. This follows director Finkelstein's 4,000-share buy at $9.23 in May. The purchase is small but in the open market near the lows.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The May 2026 director purchase was followed by the stock drifting, not by a positive print.
findings.why_not_priced: The amount is immaterial and was public two months ago. It carries signal only, not money.
findings.independence: InsiderTrades alert (https://www.insidertrades.com/alerts/nyse-brbr-insider-buying-and-selling-2026-09-10/) reports the same filing.

findings.finding: The Q4 quarter itself is pre-guided. Implied sales are $629-669M against $653M consensus, near the midpoint. Q4 adj EBITDA margin is guided at ~10%, including ~$7M of trade spend to clear excess bottles. The Q3 call guided Q4 RTD shake volume up double digits, consumption up mid-single digits and promotion near Q2 levels. The risk is quality: margins came in below guidance in Q2 and Q3 (two inventory charges totalling $21.3M), so another charge or a margin below 10% is the downside.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q3: revenue beat (+1.6%) with EPS miss and guide cut, -1.5%. Q2: -38.8% on margin and guide. Revenue beats have not been paid for on this name.
findings.why_not_priced: Mostly priced: consensus sits inside the company's guided range. The unpriced part is the record of margins missing the guide two quarters running. A clean 10% would be read as the trough being in.
findings.independence: The Q3 call transcript (https://www.webull.com/news/15385459541566464) carries the Q4 volume and promotion commentary. Same company source.

findings.finding: Joint Juice consumer settlements of $90M ($19.2M California federal + $70.8M multistate) were expected to be paid in Q4. That takes net leverage to ~4x, from 3.2x at Q3 and 2.1x a year earlier. No refinancing or covenant 8-K has been filed since 2026-08-04, and buybacks (4.9M shares at $27.41 average in 9M FY26) are likely paused. This is a cash use, not distress, but it weighs on FY27 interest and on capital return.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No sourced reaction to a leverage or settlement line on this name.
findings.why_not_priced: Largely priced: the ~4x leverage was guided on the Q3 call. What is open is whether management talks up deleveraging over buybacks in the FY27 framework.
findings.independence: Q3 call (https://www.webull.com/news/15385459541566464): 'sizable legal settlement payment' in Q4, ~4x at year-end.

outside_window.finding: Post Holdings (former parent, same Nov fiscal-year cadence) reports Q4 FY26 after the close on 2026-11-19, after this window. It gives no read-through before the BRBR exit.

baseline_tension: Skew is unusable and the put/call OI is call-heavy. The run-up (+14.7%/20d) cuts against a long, while the sell-side reset and the rising short support one. Net, the evidence neither agrees nor disagrees with a market whose only clear statement is a ~17% move in either direction, so p_up sits at 52.
lessons_applied: nothing changed: the draft already sized the FY27-guide finding small because its bar has a single source (rule 6), kept negatives small against a rising short (rule 7), kept the peer and Glanbia proxies small (rule 5), held p_up near 50 because this name has not paid for beats (rule 1), and kept abs_move at the implied move (rule 8)
